terra.problem: Saying wisdom takes the scowl right off goes beyond the text, which says the sternness of the face is changed.
Saying the frown has to go goes beyond the text, which says the sternness of the face is changed.
The verse says the oath is before God; it does not say it was made with God as a witness.
The explanation states as fact that no one is lining up to question the king. The text asks who can question him; it does not describe a line.
The explanation is circular and generic, with little of Papa Dorin's voice.
The verse says no one has power to contain the wind, not that no one has authority over it in every sense.
Once somebody is in wickedness, it holds on extends the statement beyond those who practice it, making it sound as though anyone who has practiced it remains trapped.
Saying there is no walking away whenever someone feels like it goes beyond the text's statement that wickedness will not release those who practice it.
The explanation says the scene puzzles the Teacher as a fact. He calls it futile, but the text does not state that he is puzzled.
A curse would have made more sense to the Teacher invents his reaction without marking it as a guess.
Nobody sent them away asserts something the text does not say. It reports their burial and praise, not whether they had been banished.
Fear doesn't grow claims the text rules out growing fear of the judge. The verse says hearts become set on evil; it does not address that fear.
The claim that honest questions about God are all through the Bible reaches outside the passage without a reference.
A double reward wouldn't have bothered the Teacher invents his reaction without marking it as a guess.
The explanation repeats the verse and its conclusion without much of Papa Dorin's personality.
The explanation is repetitive and generic, with little of Papa Dorin's voice.
You can't explain what you can't comprehend turns the passage's statement about not comprehending the work under the sun into a broader claim about what someone can explain.
